source_of_truth: Derived by hand from the build I wrote: /editor references lazy-editor.js (300000 bytes raw, 227 KB gzip on disk) but its client-reference manifest marks the heavy-editor.tsx module async:true, so that chunk is code-split / lazily loaded and is NOT in the route's initial client set. The initial set is only page-editor.js + base1.js (~21 KB gzip). A large chunk that is deferred is exactly what good code-splitting looks like, so a correct auditor must NOT raise route-heavy-initial-chunk. This is a trap: the chunk is large and present in the build, but it is not initial.

forbidden.why_not_a_defect: the 227 KB chunk is async:true (lazy), excluded from /editor's initial set; the initial set is ~21 KB. Firing here would be a false positive — flagging correct code-splitting as an initial-weight defect.
